question: What is the max robot size at the start of a match?
expected_answer: 18 in x 18 in x 18 in (R102)

question: How big can our robot get once it expands?
expected_answer: 18 in by 24 in by 29 in tall when fully expanded (R105)

question: Is there a weight limit for the robot?
expected_answer: No explicit weight limit (R104)

question: How many motors and servos can we use?
expected_answer: Up to 8 motors and 8 servos across all mechanisms and configurations (R503)

question: If we swap mechanisms between matches do both count toward the motor limit?
expected_answer: Yes. All configurations used at an event count toward the total (R503, I302)

question: Can we use two batteries on the robot?
expected_answer: No. Exactly 1 approved 12V NiMH main battery (R601)

question: Can we change the connector on our battery?
expected_answer: Yes. Connectors may be replaced with popular connectors like Anderson Powerpole or XT30 of comparable rating (R601)

question: Can we use an extra Expansion Hub?
expected_answer: Yes, no more than one additional REV Expansion Hub (R701)

question: What can we plug into USB on the control system?
expected_answer: Webcams and optical vision sensors, a USB hub or switch, and a REV Expansion Hub (R707)

question: Can we use a stereo camera?
expected_answer: No. Only single image sensor devices natively supported by the Robot Controller app (R708)

question: Are lasers legal?
expected_answer: Only if part of a sensor, Class I or Exempt, and non-visible (R710)

question: Can we use pneumatics?
expected_answer: No pneumatic actuators. Only sealed COTS pre-charged closed-air systems such as gas shocks (R801)

question: Can we reuse last year's code?
expected_answer: Yes. Software, designs and fabricated items made before Kickoff are permitted (R304)

question: How big do robot signs need to be and how many?
expected_answer: At least 2, minimum 6.5 in wide and 2.5 in tall, on surfaces at least 90 degrees apart (R401)

question: Can we use season game pieces as part of the robot?
expected_answer: No. Scoring elements and replicas are not allowed in construction (R305)

question: How long is auto and how long is teleop?
expected_answer: 30 seconds of AUTO and 2 minutes of TELEOP

question: Do we have to pick an OpMode if we have no auto?
expected_answer: Yes. Teams must select and INIT an OpMode regardless (G305)

question: Can we touch the driver station during auto?
expected_answer: No, except start, stop, or for safety (G401)

question: Can the robot move between auto and teleop?
expected_answer: No powered movement. Inertia, gravity or de-energizing is not a violation (G403)

question: How many game pieces can the robot hold at once?
expected_answer: No more than 4 scoring elements (G407)

question: When can we score nectar in the flowers?
expected_answer: Only in the last 60 seconds of the match (G410)

question: When can the human player put nectar on the field?
expected_answer: When 60 seconds or less remain, or one extra each time their alliance HIVE is TIPPED (G426)

question: How long can we pin another robot?
expected_answer: No more than 3 seconds (G421)

question: Can our drive coach hold the gamepad during a match?
What happens if we do not show up to a qual match?
expected_answer: If the robot passed initial inspection and no drive team member reports, DISQUALIFIED from that match (G203)

question: How many people can talk to the head ref?
expected_answer: Up to 2, one of whom must be a student (T301)

question: How long do we have to dispute a qualification match?
expected_answer: Any time before alliance selection begins, or within 5 minutes of the last qual match at events without playoffs (T302)

question: How much break do we get between back to back matches?
expected_answer: At least 5 minutes in quals and 8 minutes in playoffs (T406)

question: Can we pick a team that already declined someone else?
Do we get a backup team in playoffs?
What are bulk reads and why use them?
expected_answer: A LynxCommand that reads all non-I2C sensor values on a hub at once, saving loop time

question: Do I need RUN_USING_ENCODER for encoders to work?
expected_answer: No, it is a common misunderstanding that the mode is required just to read encoders

question: How do I get the list of connected hubs in code?
expected_answer: hardwareMap.getAll(LynxModule.class)

question: How much current is my hub pulling?
expected_answer: Use getCurrent() on the LynxModule

question: What I2C speeds does the REV hub support?
expected_answer: 100 kHz and 400 kHz

question: Should I multithread hardware calls?
expected_answer: At best ineffective, because LynxCommands are blocking with a master lock on each USB device

question: Where does my Pinpoint plug in?
expected_answer: An I2C port other than port 0, because the built-in IMU uses port 0

question: Which Pinpoint ports do the odometry pods use?
expected_answer: Forward pod in the x port, strafe pod in the y port

question: What is the difference between mecanum and omni wheels?
expected_answer: Omni rollers are at 90 degrees to wheel rotation, mecanum rollers are generally 45 degrees

question: Should dead wheels be spring loaded?
expected_answer: Yes, spring tensioning is highly recommended to keep them in contact with the ground

question: Where do I plug in the Limelight 3A?
expected_answer: USB 3.0 port (blue) on the Control Hub

question: Which REV Hardware Client should I use?
expected_answer: REV Hardware Client 2. The original has reached end of life

question: What is PLA good for on a robot?
expected_answer: Easy to print and good for fit checks and prototypes. It can soften with heat and be less suitable for impact

question: Do all servos on a hub share 5V?
expected_answer: 5V power is shared between pairs of ports
